_about: ECONOMY FOUR 11/27, VAMILY rule 489(b) (ARMORY 3's new guns, drones and rounds 'in the one price table'), ECONOMY THREE's handoff job 3 ('bands from the research: real street prices in working days at four AA a day, as the implants were priced'; rounds stay scarce, rule 478). What each of ARMORY 3's pieces really cost before the crash, in US dollars, turned into AA the way records/target/bb/implants.json does: median US working days (BLS, $1,214 a week, $243 a day, Q3 2025) at four AA a day. The game's price is the weapons table's (records/target/bb/weapons.json value, crowns at ten to one: the catalog rule of records/target/bb/battery_table.json). The gate (gates/the_new_guns_priced_gate.js) holds each piece inside its band or on the HELD list with its reason, and the HELD list may only shrink. Research and the ladder: records/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_FOUR_THE_NEW_GUNS_PRICED_11_27_26.md.

day_usd.source: BLS usual weekly earnings, full-time, median $1,214, Q3 2025 (the implants' own figure, records/target/bb/implants.json)

aa_a_day.source: records/target/bb/implants.json: four AA a skilled day (a hired man is paid 1 to 4 a night)

bands.unit: the game's price over the real one, lowest and highest
bands.source: ARMORY 3's research (records/BOHEMIA_ARMORY_THREE_THE_GUNS_GROW_UP_AND_THE_DRONE_11_27_26.md): 393 million guns and 32 million semi-automatic rifles in America, so a civilian gun is common and carries only the collapse's premium (rule 489(a): 'what runs short is the ammunition'); select-fire, belt-fed, rockets and military optics were never sold to civilians or only under the NFA, so they carry a scarcity premium; rule 489(b) calls the charge drone 'the cheap first-person drone'
bands.why: a gun the valley owns by the million costs at most four times what it did; one the army had costs up to eight; a drone you burn stays cheap

pipe_smg.real: a homemade Luty-pattern SMG: tube, sheet steel and a spring, about $300 worked

ranch_ar.real: an AR-15 off a gun store wall, about $800

pieces.source: [general knowledge] US retail and reported prices 2024-26 (each piece's 'real'); ARMORY 3's record for what each piece is; the military unit costs are the Army's purchase prices, the black market's the war markets' reported range
pieces.why: the real thing first; the game's number answers to it

worn_share.source: records/target/bb/armory.json worn value_pct 55 ('a little over half the price (a used gun's)')
worn_share.why: a beat-up gun is a little over half the clean one's price

rocket_usd.source: [general knowledge] a PG-7V rocket on the war markets, about $100 to $300
rocket_usd.why: a rocket refills from the crew's rounds at per_shot (armory.json fire), so its price is that many rounds at the stall's six for one AA

rounds_usd.source: [general knowledge] 9 mm, 5.56 and 7.62x39 about 30 to 50 cents a round retail before the crash
rounds_usd.why: six rounds were about $2.40; the stall's six for one AA is the scarcity (rule 478: what runs short is the ammunition)

value.auto_shotgun: the shotgun family sits at Battle Brothers' handgonne, its only firearm and an end-game piece (the smith's plain shotgun is 388); a real semi-auto 12 gauge is about 20 AA. Realism first says bring the family down; that moves every shotgun's place in the game and is TUNING's research and his call, not this lane's alone
value.rocket_launcher: the handgonne's price made a rocket (armory.json between handgonne and the spiked impaler); 250 against a black-market RPG-7's about 20 AA, past the rare band's eight times. The same family question as the shotguns
value.double_shotgun: the shotgun family again: 40 against a real side-by-side's about 8 AA, just over the civilian band's four times

held.source: this lane, 11/27: the pieces outside their band and why they were not moved this round
held.why: a held piece is named, never hidden; the list may only get shorter
